title: Voice Cloning & Voice Conversion
service: CloneGate: consent-gated kNN-VC voice conversion with a blind spread-spectrum watermark carrying the consent id

parts.lesson_anchor: The ethics bit, not a bolt-on (watermarking); Step 4 embed a watermark; code/main.py watermark, detect_watermark, bit_accuracy
planted_bugs: Watermarker.chips() draws from one random.Random built in __init__, so the chip sequence is not reset per call; the failure surfaces in a separate verifier reading the second clip the stamper marked
Evidence.scores() returns raw correlations instead of dividing by the root energy of each bit's samples, so scores scale with playback volume
bit_accuracy divides by the number of decided bits, dropping bits without evidence from the denominator (and dividing by zero when none is decided)
Evidence.add re-correlates the whole received audio on every call, O(N^2/chunk) for a chunked feed
parts.timing_assert: 2 s clip fed in 480 uneven chunks under 0.05 s (re-correlating version takes about 0.75 s, incremental about 3 ms)
parts.overfix_guard: detection is blind: a separate verifier with only the clip and the key must decode it (the lesson's non-blind subtract-the-original detector fails); a chunked feed must match a single feed (resetting the chips at every add fails); two evidences fed in turn must each decode their own clip (reseeding one shared RNG at every call fails)

deviations: Part 1: the timing defect is the streaming accumulator re-correlating all received audio on every add (O(N^2/chunk)); the blind-detection guard is a separate verifier instance that never saw the original, plus a chunked feed that rules out restarting the chips at every add, and two streams checked at once, which rule out reseeding one shared RNG

Part 3: the matching set is narrower than 'the target speaker': only frames enrolled under the consent that authorizes the conversion, so the consent decides which data is used (The ethics bit, not a bolt-on); alice's second consent also covers dubbing, so pooling every active consent of hers fails; the conversion averages k nearest frames as in the kNN-VC paper, while the lesson text says the single nearest

Part 4: evidence is accumulated as soft correlation and energy per bit (Part 1's z-scores) rather than hard per-chunk bit votes, because summed evidence is the optimal statistic and does not depend on chunk size; the wire format is Server-Sent Events, scored every 0.1 s of stream time and once at the end
